plan2.title: What people clock in ten seconds

strong.text:
Yeon's add-on for strong charts: whatever first impression you make, it lands harder than you think. You walk in with a fully formed opinion of the room, and the room can feel it. Some people find that magnetic. Others decide in ten seconds that you're a lot, and they never tell you, they just sit at the other end of the table.

Try one experiment at your next new-people event. Ask three questions before you share one opinion. Not interview questions, curious ones. What are you into lately? How do you know the host? You'll still make your impression. It'll just include the information that you're interested in other people, which is the part strong charts accidentally leave out. Same you, better reviews.

Also, check your face. Strong charts often have a resting expression that says "I've already decided about you." You haven't, usually. You're just thinking. But people read faces before they hear a word. Relax your jaw, look at whoever is talking, nod once in a while. Tiny adjustments, huge difference in how many people come over to talk to you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Three questions before one opinion. Try it once. Watch the room relax.

weak.text:
Yeon's add-on for weak charts: you make the impression above and then undercut it. A nervous joke, an apology for talking, a quick retreat into the polite, agreeable version of you. People assume that's the whole show. Months later they discover how funny and opinionated you really are, and they feel a bit cheated, like they got the trailer for a different film.

Try leading with one real thing. A strong opinion about something low-stakes, pineapple on pizza, the best season, which friend in the group would survive a horror movie. Small, specific, yours. Weak charts hold back the good stuff until they feel safe. Let a little out early. The right people will find you faster, and the wrong ones were never going to get the director's cut anyway.

And stop apologizing for taking up the first thirty seconds. Weak charts introduce themselves like they're interrupting: "Hi, sorry, I'm, um, a friend of Sam's." Try "Hi, I'm" and your name, said like it's good news. It is good news. You're about to be one of the more interesting people they meet tonight.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Lead with one real opinion. Pizza counts. Stop handing out the trailer version.

base.first-impression: Okay, Gap. Here's what people clock in the first ten seconds: confidence, opinions, and posture like you're about to give a talk nobody booked. You walk in like the room should rearrange itself around you. Half the time it does, which is annoying for everyone else and great for you. People assume you're in charge, so they hand you things: projects, problems, the restaurant booking. You take them, obviously. What they don't see right away is that you're quite sensitive about being respected. You'd rather be right than liked. You'd prefer both. And you get grumpy when you can only pick one. That's the read. You're welcome.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: Gap. Gap enters a party like it's a board meeting.

base_panels.speaker: bom
base_panels.text: That's called leadership, Yeon.

base_panels.speaker: yeon
base_panels.text: It's called refusing to let anyone else pick the restaurant.

spring.intro:
Spring Gap Wood, let's be honest. You were born when Wood ran the whole season, so you got a double helping of yourself: upright, principled and absolutely convinced you're right. People clock it in ten seconds. You stand like the podium is already yours. Your red flag is treating disagreement like a structural threat. Someone suggests another restaurant and you defend your choice like it's a load-bearing wall. Your friends love that you're reliable. They also have a group chat where they decide things before telling you. The fix is boring and effective: lose one argument a week on purpose and watch nothing collapse.

Yeon's seasonal note: spring babies start things with enormous enthusiasm and abandon about half of them by June. Before you start the next big thing, finish one small old thing. Just one.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You defended your restaurant choice like a thesis. It was a sandwich place.

summer.intro:
Summer Gap, you arrived when Fire ran things, and Wood exists to feed Fire. Translation: you're a giver who can't stop giving opinions, plans, help and unsolicited life advice. You show love by volunteering for everything. The red flag is that you burn yourself out and then quietly resent everyone for letting you. Nobody asked you to organize the group holiday, plan the birthday and fix your friend's résumé in one week. You offered. Then you sighed loudly about it. Bom says you're generous. You are. You're also a martyr with a calendar. Stop offering things you don't want to do, and the resentment has nothing to eat.

Yeon's seasonal note: summer babies run hot. Big feelings, big plans, big crashes. Schedule the crash: one lazy day a week, on purpose, so it doesn't schedule itself at the worst time.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You volunteered for three things, then sighed about all three. Pick one, Gap.

autumn.intro:
Autumn Gap, your season belonged to Metal and Metal is the axe to your tree. So you grew up with a strict inner critic and turned it into a personality. You judge yourself hard and, surprise, you judge everyone else by the same rulebook. People notice the raised eyebrow before you say a word. Your red flag is calling it having standards when sometimes it's just being harsh. In love you prune people: one mistake and they're off the shortlist. At work you're the person who corrects the slide deck during the meeting. The fix: before you judge, ask one curious question. Shocking how often it changes the verdict.

Yeon's seasonal note: autumn babies judge. Gently, accurately, constantly. Give one person a pass this week they haven't technically earned. It's good practice.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You corrected a typo in someone's birthday message. In the group chat. Publicly.

winter.intro:
Winter-born Gap: Water ran the season and Water feeds Wood, so you've got deep roots and the patience of a glacier. Nice. Also: you overthink everything and call it being thorough. People see a calm, solid person. Your friends know you need three business days to reply to pizza or Thai. Your red flag is stubborn stillness: you won't move until you're absolutely certain, and you're rarely absolutely certain. In love you wait for perfect conditions that don't exist. At work you research a decision until it's out of date. The fix is a rule: small choices get five minutes. Roots are great. Trees still have to grow.

Yeon's seasonal note: winter babies hibernate and call it being busy. People miss you. Go outside, see a friend, reply to the thing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pizza or Thai should not require a pros and cons list, Gap.

earth.intro:
Born in the Earth days, Gap, the end-of-season weeks when the ground takes over. Wood controls Earth, so you grew up managing terrain: chores, plans, other people's half-finished ideas. People see a capable leader. Your friends see someone who turns a picnic into a project. Your red flag is treating people like ground to be organized. In love, partners feel scheduled. At work, you volunteer for everything and resent it quietly by Thursday. The fix: let one thing stay messy this week and don't touch it. The field survives.

Yeon's seasonal note: Earth-days babies absorb everyone's mood and call it being supportive. Some of it is just sponging. Wring yourself out regularly.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Not everything is a project, Gap. Some things are just Tuesday.

three-people.heading: What three people would say, if they were brave
three-people.text: What three people would say about you, Gap, if they were brave. Your ex: "Amazing in a crisis, impossible in an argument." Your coworker: "Gets things done. Also redid my slides without asking." Your best friend: "The most loyal person I know, and they will tell you what to do with your life whether you asked or not." All three love you a bit. All three would like you to ask more questions.

cliff.text: Your red flag? You don't bend. At all. A tree grows straight up, and you've decided that's a personality trait instead of a botanical fact.

sample.text: You plan the dates, the trips, the five-year outline nobody asked to see.

base.first-impression: Eul, people meet you and think: oh, they're lovely. Easy to talk to, warm, funny, somehow already on first-name terms with the barista. You read rooms like a professional and adjust in real time. Ten seconds in, people feel comfortable. Ten minutes in, they've told you about their childhood and their ex. What they don't notice is that you're also quietly checking whether they like you. Constantly. You're charming partly because you're working at it, a little, all the time. Which is fine. Just know that it's work, and you're allowed to clock out whenever you like.

spring.intro:
Spring Eul, your season belonged to Wood and doubled your element, so you're a vine in a garden full of things to climb. You're charming, adaptable and know everyone. People clock you as the friend who's friends with the bartender in ten minutes. The red flag: you're so good at fitting in that nobody knows what you actually think. You agree with whoever's closest. Your opinion on a film changes depending on who you watched it with. In love you become their taste, their music, their friends. The fix: keep one opinion this week that nobody else in the room shares, and say it out loud. Yes, it will feel weird.

Yeon's seasonal note: spring babies start things with enormous enthusiasm and abandon about half of them by June. Before you start the next big thing, finish one small old thing. Just one.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You loved that film with one friend and hated it with another. Same film.

summer.intro:
Summer Eul, Fire ran things when you were born and Wood feeds Fire, so your energy flows out as charm. You're the flower that blooms for an audience, and honey, you love an audience. People notice your vibe instantly: warm, cute, effortlessly social. What they also notice is how often you check whether everyone's having fun, including whether they're watching you have fun. Your red flag is performing ease. You look relaxed in every photo and exhausted in every taxi home. In love you hide your needs to stay the low-effort option. The fix: stop caring whether you're liked for one whole evening. Sit in a corner. Survive.

Yeon's seasonal note: summer babies run hot. Big feelings, big plans, big crashes. Schedule the crash: one lazy day a week, on purpose, so it doesn't schedule itself at the worst time.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You checked if everyone was having fun nine times. Were you, though?

autumn.intro:
Autumn Eul, your season belonged to Metal and Metal cuts Wood. So you grew up reading the room like your survival depended on it, and now you're a professional mood detector. Impressive skill. Terrible habit. People see someone sweet and accommodating. Your friends know you'll say you don't mind and then mind enormously. Your red flag is passive resilience: you bend, bend, bend, then quietly leave without explaining. In love that means one day you're just gone, and they genuinely have no idea why. At work you take on extra tasks and seethe. The fix: say 'actually, I mind' once a week. Out loud. To a human.

Yeon's seasonal note: autumn babies judge. Gently, accurately, constantly. Give one person a pass this week they haven't technically earned. It's good practice.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: 'I don't mind,' says Eul, minding it with every single cell.

winter.intro:
Winter-born Eul: Water ran the season and feeds your Wood, so you're a bulb that keeps its flower hidden until it's sure. You're quietly perceptive and secretly intense. People think you're shy or easygoing. They have no idea you've already formed detailed opinions about everyone at the table. Your red flag is keeping your inner life so private that people misjudge you, and then being hurt that they misjudged you. In love you wait to be discovered instead of letting yourself be known. At work your best ideas stay in your notes app. The fix: share one thought before you've polished it. People can't water what they can't see.

Yeon's seasonal note: winter babies hibernate and call it being busy. People miss you. Go outside, see a friend, reply to the thing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your notes app has better ideas than the whole meeting. Say one, Eul.

earth.intro:
Here's the deal, Eul: you arrived in the Earth days, a vine on hard ground, and you learned to get around every obstacle without ever asking it to move. People think you're easygoing. Your friends know you've already found three workarounds and told nobody. Your red flag is quiet maneuvering. In love you steer instead of asking. At work you get your way so smoothly that nobody remembers agreeing. The fix: ask for one thing directly this week, in a full sentence, with no hint attached.

Yeon's seasonal note: Earth-days babies absorb everyone's mood and call it being supportive. Some of it is just sponging. Wring yourself out regularly.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Eul gets there every time. Imagine how fast it'd be in a straight line!

three-people.heading: What three people would say, if they were brave
three-people.text: What three people would say about you, Eul, if they were brave. Your ex: "So sweet. I never knew what they actually wanted." Your coworker: "Everyone likes them. Nobody knows their opinion on anything." Your best friend: "Would cross the city for me, then say 'it was on the way.'" All three would love to see more of the real you, opinions included.

cliff.text: Your red flag: you're a professional chameleon. You become whatever the person in front of you seems to want, and you're so good at it that you sometimes forget your own color.

sample.text: In love you wrap around people like a vine around a fence, and then wonder why you can't leave the fence.

base.first-impression: Byeong, you don't enter a room, you happen to it. Ten seconds in, people know your name, your opinion on the playlist, and that you're the fun one. You're warm, generous, a little loud, and genuinely delightful. People feel seen by you, which is your real magic. What they also clock: you need an audience. Not in a bad way. You just light up when people are watching and dim slightly when they're not. That isn't vanity. That's a sun noticing it's daytime. Still, it's worth knowing that everyone can tell when you're on.

spring.intro:
Spring Byeong, your season belonged to Wood and feeds your Fire, so you've got unlimited fuel and you use all of it. You're the friend who turns a quiet Tuesday into an event. People clock you as fun, loud and probably the one who suggested shots. Your red flag is optimism used as avoidance. Problem at work? It'll be fine. Friend upset? Let's go out. Relationship wobbling? Let's book a trip. You'd rather add sunshine than look at the crack. Bom loves that about you. I love it too, mostly. The fix: when something's wrong, sit with it for ten minutes before you try to cheer it up.

Yeon's seasonal note: spring babies start things with enormous enthusiasm and abandon about half of them by June. Before you start the next big thing, finish one small old thing. Just one.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Booking a weekend away is not how you fix an argument, Byeong.

summer.intro:
Summer-born Byeong: Fire ran the season and doubled your element. You're the sun at noon, which means you're glorious and a little hard to look at directly. People know you're in the room before they see you. The red flag: everything is about the energy, and the energy is about you. You don't mean to make it your show. It just becomes your show. Friends tell a story, you tell a bigger one. In love you're passionate and then suddenly bored the second it gets ordinary. At work you start five projects and finish two. The fix: ask one follow-up question before you share your own story. Let someone else be the weather.

Yeon's seasonal note: summer babies run hot. Big feelings, big plans, big crashes. Schedule the crash: one lazy day a week, on purpose, so it doesn't schedule itself at the worst time.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your friend got engaged and you told the story of your holiday. Byeong. Please.

autumn.intro:
Autumn Byeong, you were born while Metal was in charge and Fire's job is to work Metal, so you're a sun with a to-do list. Warm, and also weirdly competitive. People see someone generous and capable. Your friends know you keep score: who planned the last dinner, who paid, who texted first. Your red flag is turning love into a project you can win. In relationships you try to fix your partner like a renovation. At work you'll take over a task because you'd do it better, and you might, but now everyone feels useless. The fix: let something be done badly by someone else. Clap anyway. That's real warmth.

Yeon's seasonal note: autumn babies judge. Gently, accurately, constantly. Give one person a pass this week they haven't technically earned. It's good practice.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You've kept a mental tally of who paid for brunch since 2023. Byeong.

winter.intro:
Winter Byeong, Water ran your birth season and Water puts out Fire. So you shine like someone who's had to fight for it, a little too bright and a little too fast. People see the life of the party. Your friends know you leave early, go home and lie on the floor. Your red flag is performing happiness so nobody sees you dim. You'll say you're great with your whole chest while running on empty. In love you hide the cold days until they become a cold month. At work you overcommit to look on top of it. The fix: tell one person you're tired and don't follow it with a joke.

Yeon's seasonal note: winter babies hibernate and call it being busy. People miss you. Go outside, see a friend, reply to the thing.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're allowed to be cloudy sometimes, Byeong. We still like you.

earth.intro:
Earth days close every season, and you were born in them, Byeong. Fire feeds Earth, so your heat goes straight into other people's ground. You host, you cheer, you fix the mood. People see sunshine. Your friends see someone who never admits being tired. Your red flag is generosity with a hidden invoice. In love you give so much that you start keeping score in secret. At work you take on the morale of the whole team. The fix: say no to one favor this week, warmly, without a reason.

Yeon's seasonal note: Earth-days babies absorb everyone's mood and call it being supportive. Some of it is just sponging. Wring yourself out regularly.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The sun doesn't send invoices, Byeong. Stop doing it in your head.

three-people.heading: What three people would say, if they were brave
three-people.text: What three people would say about you, Byeong, if they were brave. Your ex: "The most fun I've ever had, and the most tired I've ever been." Your coworker: "Lights up every meeting. Also makes every meeting longer." Your best friend: "Would throw me the best party of my life, then forget to text back for a week." All three adore you. All three want a little more follow-through.

cliff.text: Red flag, Byeong: you overshare, overcommit and overexplain, all before lunch. You say yes to every plan because you love people, then cancel two of them because you're exhausted.

sample.text: With someone you love, you go big and fast.

base.first-impression: Jeong, people meet you and feel like you're paying attention. Because you are. Ten seconds in, you've noticed their mood, their nervous hands, and that the person beside them is lying about something. You're warm but not loud, a candle rather than a bonfire. People feel safe telling you things. What they don't see: you're also deciding whether they're safe for you. And most of them don't pass. You're friendly with many and close to very few, and the few have no idea how hard the exam was. Maybe make the exam a little easier.

spring.intro:
Spring Jeong, you were born while Wood was in charge, and Wood feeds your candle, so you've got plenty of emotional fuel and you burn it on one subject at a time. Currently that's probably a person, a show or a grudge. People see someone soft, attentive and lovely. They don't see the archive. You remember everything: what they said, how they said it, and the date. Your red flag is keeping receipts in your heart and bringing them out months later. In love you're devoted and secretly keeping score. At work you're the quiet one who notices every slight. The fix: say it within forty-eight hours or let it go. No more vintage grievances.

Yeon's seasonal note: spring babies start things with enormous enthusiasm and abandon about half of them by June. Before you start the next big thing, finish one small old thing. Just one.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You brought up something from eighteen months ago. With the exact quote. Jeong.

summer.intro:
Summer Jeong, Fire ran your season and doubled your element, so your candle burns at bonfire intensity in a very small space. You're loyal, fierce and deeply private. People see someone warm and composed. Your close friends know that when you're hurt, you go silent and the room drops ten degrees. Your red flag is the cold shoulder delivered with burning eyes. You'd rather simmer than say it. In love you're all in, then all hurt, and they have to guess why. At work you'll defend your people fiercely and freeze out anyone who crossed them. The fix: words before silence. Every single time.

Yeon's seasonal note: summer babies run hot. Big feelings, big plans, big crashes. Schedule the crash: one lazy day a week, on purpose, so it doesn't schedule itself at the worst time.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The silent treatment is a candle pretending to be an ice cube, Jeong.

autumn.intro:
Autumn Jeong, you were born while Metal was in charge, and your flame's job is to shape Metal. So you're a perfectionist who calls it attention to detail. People see someone thoughtful who gives the best gifts. Your friends know you've redone your grid twice this year. Your red flag is quiet control: you want things just so, and you'll adjust them yourself rather than ask. In love you might gently edit your partner: their clothes, their phrasing, their plans. At work you quietly reformat everyone else's document. The fix: let one thing stay imperfect and see if anyone notices. Nobody will. That's the lesson.

Yeon's seasonal note: autumn babies judge. Gently, accurately, constantly. Give one person a pass this week they haven't technically earned. It's good practice.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You reformatted the shared doc at midnight. Nobody asked, Jeong. Nobody.

winter.intro:
Winter Jeong, Water ran your season and Water puts out Fire, so you guard your little flame like it's the last match on earth. You're intuitive, warm in private and suspicious in public. People find you hard to read, and you like it that way. Your red flag is testing people instead of trusting them. You drop hints, see who picks them up and quietly grade the results. In love you protect yourself so carefully that partners feel like they're auditioning. At work you won't ask for help in case you look weak. The fix: tell someone what you need directly, once. No test, no hint, no secret score.

Yeon's seasonal note: winter babies hibernate and call it being busy. People miss you. Go outside, see a friend, reply to the thing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Hinting, then grading who noticed, is a game nobody knows they're playing, Jeong.

earth.intro:
You were born in the Earth days, Jeong, a candle in a clay room. Your warmth stays close and the room keeps it. People see someone calm and cozy. Your friends know you notice everything and file it away for later. Your red flag is keeping quiet now and keeping the receipts forever. In love, a hurt from months ago comes out in one perfect sentence. At work you absorb problems instead of raising them. The fix: say small things while they're small. Today, not in October.

Yeon's seasonal note: Earth-days babies absorb everyone's mood and call it being supportive. Some of it is just sponging. Wring yourself out regularly.

You could, and you have, several times, without making a fuss. You don't perform, don't oversell, don't rush. What they also clock: you're hard to read. Is Mu happy? Annoyed? Asleep with eyes open? Nobody knows. Not even, on some days, you. You've perfected the neutral face so well that you sometimes forget there's weather behind it. Let someone in on the forecast sometimes.

You let people put roots through you and then act shocked when you crack. In love you go along with their plans until you suddenly don't. At work you absorb extra tasks without a word. summer.intro:
Summer Mu, your season belonged to Fire and Fire feeds Earth, so you're a sun-warmed mountain: solid, confident and completely unwilling to move. People clock you as dependable. Then they try to change the plan. Your red flag is stubbornness wearing a calm face. You don't argue. You simply don't budge, and somehow that's worse. In love partners feel like they're negotiating with geography. At work you're reliable and also the reason the new system took nine months to roll out. The fix: when someone suggests a change, say let's try it before you say but. You'll still be a mountain afterward. Promise.

Yeon's seasonal note: summer babies run hot. Big feelings, big plans, big crashes. Schedule the crash: one lazy day a week, on purpose, so it doesn't schedule itself at the worst time.

autumn.intro:
Autumn Mu, Metal was in command when you arrived and Earth gives birth to Metal, so you express yourself through doing. You're the friend who helps you move flat and then says nothing about your feelings, ever. People see someone useful and kind. Your friends know you'd rather assemble furniture than have one emotional conversation. Your red flag is acts of service as a hiding place. In love you show care with deeds and dodge every talk about what it means. At work you're the workhorse nobody thinks to promote because you never ask. The fix: say one feeling out loud this week. Not a fact. A feeling. I'll wait.

Yeon's seasonal note: autumn babies judge. Gently, accurately, constantly. Give one person a pass this week they haven't technically earned. It's good practice.

panel.text: You built their entire wardrobe and said zero feelings. Typical Mu love letter.

winter.intro:
Winter Mu, your season belonged to Water and Earth controls Water, so you're a dam with a calm face. You manage everyone's emotions, including your own, mostly by not having them in public. People see the steady one. Your friends call you in a crisis because you won't panic. Your red flag is control dressed up as calm. You decide what counts as an overreaction, including other people's. In love partners feel handled rather than met. At work you keep the peace so firmly that problems never get named. The fix: let somebody else's feelings be messy without managing them. Just listen. Don't fix. Don't shrink it.

Yeon's seasonal note: winter babies hibernate and call it being busy. People miss you. Go outside, see a friend, reply to the thing.

panel.text: Mu is the calm in every storm. It's okay to have a storm sometimes.

earth.intro:
Earth days are Earth's own season, Mu, and you got a double helping. Mountain on mountain. People see someone solid and reliable. Your friends see someone who decided in 2019 and hasn't revisited. Your red flag is immovability passing as calm. In love partners feel like they're negotiating with geography. At work your no is final before anyone finishes the pitch. The fix: change one small opinion this month, on purpose, and notice that the mountain is still standing.
